findings.title: Exact zero displacement is incorrectly treated as an unstable solve
findings.evidence: When mu0 equals the sample mean, delta, z and solution are zero. The normalized residual is then 0/(0+0), hence NaN; the function returns NOT_EVALUABLE even with positive definite covariance. A centered scalar sample [-1,1] is a static minimal witness. No witness was executed because reanalysis was prohibited.
findings.consequence: The generic routine mishandles a valid centered mean or a null set to the sample mean; this is false abstention rather than false detection. Current sealed invocation has nonzero mean and finite residual 8.795923874997615e-17, so the saved result is unaffected.
findings.minimal_fix: Before wider reuse, define normalized residual as 0 when finite delta and finite solution are both exactly zero after valid full-rank Cholesky; add one zero-displacement synthetic test expecting T2=0 and F-tail=1. Preserve the sealed current candidate.

findings.title: Basis validation lacks an independently specified positive complex fixture
findings.evidence: The positive check compares rows loaded using signed_alm_to_real with the same converter called again. Negative-m and m=0 corruption witnesses exist, and production norm preservation is independently compared to signed-m power, but no hand-built complex row is compared to a known ordered 42-vector.
findings.consequence: A convention/sign/order error could evade the positive test. Static inspection currently matches the frozen negative sqrt(2) imaginary convention and E/B, ell, m ordering. This does not invalidate the fixed candidate.
findings.minimal_fix: At the next authorized code change, add one hand-built valid signed-m fixture with independently specified expected coordinate positions and signs; do not claim that this stronger fixture already ran.
